note: Access points for the float/shuttle planner. Source of truth: access_points_source.csv (edit that, then re-run build_access.py). segment = a flowing reach (river=American, sacramento-river, feather-river — float + shuttle, connected as a downstream network) or a lake (lake-natoma/folsom-lake — flatwater above a dam, paddle). river_mi = miles along the reach centerline from its downstream end; flow_mi = miles to the system mouth (crosses confluences). lat/lon = water's edge; parking_lat/lon = the lot.

speed_mph.note: typical float/paddle speed at regular flows

access.name: Verona (Feather River)
access.parking_fee: $20 per launch, $10 per additional vehicle (take out?)
access.parking_info: Verona area river access, at the Feather–Sacramento confluence. Tribal owned, check website for access and fees.
access.walk_to_water: short walk to the bank
access.note: Feather River at Verona — same spot as verona-sac (Sacramento), listed on both routes so it's an option for either.

access.name: Discovery Park Boat Ramp
access.parking_info: Sac Regional Parks controlled, if you have a pass you can park for free.
access.walk_to_water: ~600 ft, across paved parking lot and down ramp to waterline
access.note: To get to this take the paddler must turn upriver at confluence and go upstream a bit to enter the cover where the boat ramp is located. Also, shuttle drivers must drive across the bridge to the boat ramp - farther than Tiscornia.

access.name: Karnak (Advanced)
access.parking_info: Park on gravel road near industrial buildings on dry side of levees. Walk over to water and put in. A Sutter County option for something between Knights Landing and the Confluence.
access.walk_to_water: Walk over levees to water and down to waterline. Steep with rip rap rocks, slippery.
access.cautions: Slippery, rocks line take out. Water is calm there, though. Property access is ambiguus, water district staff leave me alone when they see I am just boating.
